targets.old_statement: Level Two is the first level that allows driving alone, and only from 5 a.m. to 9 p.m. or when going straight to or from work or a volunteer emergency service.
targets.old_spoken_statement: Level Two is the first level that allows driving alone, and only from five a.m. to nine p.m. or when going straight to or from work or a volunteer emergency service.
targets.statement: A Level Two license holder may drive unsupervised between five a.m. and nine p.m., and at any hour when traveling straight to or from work or any volunteer fire, rescue, or emergency medical organization in which they serve.

targets.old_statement: Level Two must be held for at least six months before the Full Provisional License, which is shorter than the nine-month Level One holding period.
targets.old_spoken_statement: Level Two must be held for at least six months before the Full Provisional License, which is shorter than the nine-month Level One holding period.
targets.statement: A Level Two Limited Provisional License must be held for at least six months before applying for a Full Provisional License.

targets.old_statement: Lose Control, Lose Your License is about school discipline, more than 10 consecutive days of suspension or alternative placement, not about traffic violations.
targets.old_spoken_statement: Lose Control, Lose Your License is about school discipline, more than ten consecutive days of suspension or alternative placement, not about traffic violations.
targets.statement: Under Lose Control, Lose Your License, a student loses their license for twelve months upon receiving a suspension for more than ten consecutive days or a disciplinary assignment to an alternative educational setting for more than ten consecutive days.

targets.old_statement: A license restriction is a limit you must stay within; breaking it is not a minor infraction but counts as driving without a license.
targets.old_spoken_statement: A license restriction is a limit you must stay within; breaking it is not a minor infraction but counts as driving without a license.
targets.statement: If your driver license has a restriction, you may drive only within the limits of that restriction; otherwise the law treats you as driving without a license.
